project.name: miCareer-mini
project.description: Thin Streamlit frontend for HR and candidate recruitment workflows that delegates AI-heavy processing, ranking, and chat behavior to FANG.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit entrypoint that initializes session state, renders HR and candidate pages, and orchestrates calls to the database, FANG APIs, NMAIex APIs, and Cloudinary upload flow.

nodes.name: cloudinary_upload.py
nodes.summary: Uploads candidate CV PDFs to Cloudinary and returns the secure public URL used by local application records and FANG ingestion.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: Relational data access layer for HR login, candidate login, job listings, applications, ingestion status lookups, and candidate profile reads and writes.

nodes.name: fang_client.py
nodes.summary: Thin HTTP client for FANG chat and ingestion endpoints, including conversation history, summarization, branching, ingestion polling, and health checks.

nodes.name: nmaiex_client.py
nodes.summary: Thin HTTP client for NMAIex master data, job editing, candidate profile sync, and ranking endpoints exposed through the FANG backend.

nodes.name: test_playwright.py
nodes.summary: Manual Playwright smoke test that drives the local Streamlit UI through the HR login flow and verifies the expected landing state.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Example environment configuration for FANG API connectivity and Cloudinary credentials required by the application.

nodes.summary: Secret-scanning configuration for repository leak detection.

nodes.name: .pre-commit-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Pre-commit hook configuration used to enforce repository quality checks before changes are committed.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Analysis ignore configuration that scopes what the understand-anything graph builder includes or excludes.

nodes.name: requirements.txt
nodes.summary: Python dependency manifest for the Streamlit app, database driver, HTTP clients, Cloudinary support, and local tooling.

nodes.summary: Architecture and delivery plan that explains the intended split of responsibilities between FANG and miCareer-mini across chat, ranking, and candidate apply flows.

nodes.name: candidate_apply_strategy.md
nodes.summary: Detailed architecture strategy for candidate login, job browsing, CV upload, application creation, and FANG ingestion polling.

layers.name: Presentation And Flow
layers.description: Interactive Streamlit pages, page routing, and end-to-end user flow coordination for HR and candidate experiences.

layers.name: Integration Clients
layers.description: Adapters that call external services such as FANG, NMAIex, and Cloudinary while keeping orchestration logic out of the UI.

layers.name: Data Access
layers.description: SQL-backed relational access for users, job postings, applications, candidate profiles, and ingestion status records.

layers.name: Quality And Operations
layers.description: Local test automation and repository-level configuration that shape runtime dependencies, secret handling, quality checks, and analysis scope.

layers.name: Documentation And Planning
layers.description: Human-readable project guides, strategy notes, and planning artifacts that explain the current architecture and its intended evolution.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the project overview and architecture plan to understand why miCareer-mini is intentionally a thin UI on top of FANG.

tour.title: UI Entrypoint
tour.description: Inspect the Streamlit entrypoint that initializes session state, selects pages, and coordinates both HR and candidate workflows.

tour.title: Candidate Apply Flow
tour.description: Follow the candidate application path from UI to CV upload, application creation, and ingestion polling.

tour.title: Relational Data Backbone
tour.description: Review the database layer that supports authentication, job listing, application detail views, and candidate profile persistence.

tour.title: External Service Adapters
tour.description: Read the FANG and NMAIex clients to see how ranking, chat, ingestion, and structured-job updates are delegated to backend APIs.

tour.title: Quality And Local Validation
tour.description: Finish with the local smoke test and repo-level config to see how the team validates the UI and controls dependencies and analysis scope.
